summary_en: SHOEI YAKUHIN raised its full-year dividend forecast for fiscal 2027 (ending March 2027) to 43 yen per share from 41 yen, reflecting upward revision of net profit attributable to parent company shareholders to 588 million yen from 437 million yen, with a payout ratio of 25.1%.
title_en: Notice of Revision of Full-Year Consolidated Business Forecast and Revision of Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
SHOEI YAKUHIN announced a revision of its dividend forecast for fiscal 2027 ending March 31, 2027. The company increased the full-year dividend per share from 41 yen to 43 yen, up by 2 yen. This increase follows an upward revision of the full-year consolidated earnings forecast, with net profit attributable to parent company shareholders expected to reach 588 million yen, compared to the previously forecast 437 million yen. The payout ratio is projected at 25.1%, which exceeds the company's stated minimum target of 25% or higher.

The company cited stronger-than-expected operational performance through the second quarter ended September 2026. Notably, the chemical products business segment benefited from increased orders from domestic major customers amid supply chain risk mitigation related to Middle East geopolitical conditions. The company also achieved appropriate price pass-through amid elevated natural oil (palm oil) prices. Subsidiaries operating in China and Thailand contributed favorably, and the consumer products and civil engineering materials segments maintained steady sales momentum.

The company maintains a basic dividend policy emphasizing long-term shareholder returns through stable, progressive ordinary dividends while securing necessary internal reserves for future business development. The revised dividend of 43 yen will be formally determined by resolution at the 67th Annual General Meeting of Shareholders, scheduled for late June 2027.
